lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - A Listen, point and say

details:
Listen, point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound.
Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds and confident repetition.
“I’m sad. I really want to go outside, but our friends are all busy inside today and none of them want to come outside with me. What are they doing? Let’s find out!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connection and fine motor skills. Students practise listening for specific information and clearly circling an image.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, pencil grip and penmanship.
“Do you think Tommy might want to come outside with me? Shall we ask?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.79 - A Find and circle

details: Find and circle tests word recognition in the context of a word search puzzle.
Look for correct identification of the words and neat circling.
“Ok, maybe I’ll find something to do inside, too. Can you help me find the things I could do?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.79 - B Look and write

details: Look and write tests students’ written production of the infinitives identified in the word search and the -ing forms.
Look for correct formation of the -ing forms, correct spelling of both forms and neat handwriting between the lines.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice of the target language, in this case the present continuous in the ‘I’ and ‘you’ form, by asking and responding to simple questions.
Look for correct formation of the question and answer, particularly the -ing form and the ‘I’m’ contraction, and all students being on-task.
“Hmm, I’m bored of being inside again. Do any of you want to come outside with me? Ask and answer questions to find out.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - D. Ask and answer

details: The second ask and answer gives students  controlled practice of the ‘he’ and ‘she’ forms for the present continuous, by asking and responding to simple questions.
Look for correct formation of the question and answer, particularly the -ing form and the ‘he’s’ / ‘she’s’ contraction, and all students being on task.
“I’m going to go and play outside by myself. It seems like all our friends are busy. Can you tell me what these friends are doing?”

As well as being fun, the chant gives students the chance to practise the natural rhythms and intonation of the language in an authentic context.
Look for active participation, correct pronunciation, authentic intonation and all students participating.
“Well, I hope someone will play outside with me tomorrow!”
